title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Holiday: Thanksgiving (event week)
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted historical effect: x0.49 (2024-11-25: x0.34, 2025-11-24: x0.35); consistent with 51% drop.

drivers.name: Store closed Monday for renovation
drivers.evidence: No past data on closures; conservative estimate based on lost sales day; applied as small downside.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 10.2. Thanksgiving (event week) historically reduces sales to 49% of baseline (noise-adjusted), so a 51% downward effect is warranted. The store closure on Monday (Thanksgiving week) further reduces demand, but no past closure data exists. The price increase to $4.08 (+6%) is modest and unlikely to drive significant lift given past promotions (max 30% off) had noise-adjusted lift of x1.45. The classical model's suggestion of x0.49 aligns with historical Thanksgiving effect and is well-supported. No other drivers (e.g., promotion, competitor) are active. Confidence is medium due to limited past closure impact data.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
